name: Battle of the Kalka River
summary: At the Battle of the Kalka River (May 31, 1223), a Mongol scouting force under generals Jebe and Subutai, having already swept through the Caucasus, Georgia, and the north Caucasian steppe, confronts a joint Rus-Cuman army of perhaps 80,000. The Mongols feign retreat; the Cumans pursue and break formation; the Mongol cavalry wheels and annihilates the now-separated forces. Six Rus princes are captured; the Mongols execute them by suffocation under boards while dining on top. The Mongol force then withdraws eastward. The battle is the first contact between the Mongols and the Rus, a 17-year warning before Batu Khan's full invasion.

_quarry.structural_significance: First Mongol encounter with the Rus and Cuman forces; demonstrates Mongol tactical superiority; the withdrawal east prevents immediate conquest, giving a false sense of security; sets the stage for the full invasion of 1237–1240
